absence: Keywords beyond the governed risk title are generic business-risk vocabulary for the same entity-wide theme (see _GENERAL_RISK_KEYWORDS), not per-condition prose. Country- or condition-specific terms -- the Taiwan Layer-1 baseline -- are still not copied. Driver text is stored and is not used as a keyword.

themes.themeName: Aviation Regulatory Compliance; Quality & Safety of Products or Services
themes.sheetDetail: Compliance with aviation authorities’ regulatory requirements; poor CA product quality (e.g. product recall, Airworthiness Directives, Quality & Safety Service Bulletins); poor vendor material/services quality affecting product quality and safety (e.g. Suspected Unapproved Parts); staff lapse due to human error; reputational impact and potential liability claims from aviation incidents/accidents; FAA aviation AI regulatory roadmap and framework.
themes.sheetExtra: QMS and Aviation SMS founded on open incident reporting; vendor qualification, audit and monitoring; audits against aviation authority, aviation and ISO standards; global CA Quality & Safety Issues Management Review and cross-sharing of lessons learnt; product/services insurance; GIMS for Global IBUs (pending Hubei); SUP and counterfeit-parts controls, including strengthened supplier qualification and the Group OEST(Quality) policy; quality performance indicators; EASA, CAAS and FAA training (Parts 21, 145 and 147).
themes.sheetActionPlans: Implement GIMS in the new Hubei, China MRO; develop an anonymous incident-reporting website accessible to staff and non-staff.

themes.sheetDetail: Airlines’ cost pressure and price sensitivity; loss of competitiveness if competitors innovate, digitalise and adopt AI faster; airlines and competitors expanding across the aviation value chain through vertical or horizontal integration; competitor repair investment and capacity expansion.
themes.sheetExtra: Differentiate and bundle products/services rather than compete on price alone; CI, Kaizen, automation and digitalisation; cost-control and reduction initiatives; long-term strategic OEM partnerships; explore multi-tenant campus facilities in lower-cost regions.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Build next-generation aircraft OEM/MRO capability; implement AI/CI Execution Framework and Operational Excellence Framework; strengthen productivity through AI, automation and digitalisation to protect cost competitiveness.

themes.themeName: Geopolitical risks, global fragmentation and protectionism impacting business operation and supply chain
themes.sheetDetail: Material shortages and higher material, fuel, freight and electricity costs from sanctions, export controls and tariffs, compounded by conflict; inability to continue business with sanctioned customers; supply-chain and operational disruption from sanctions, blockades, U.S.–China competition and Middle East instability.
themes.sheetExtra: Diversify and localise supply chains; sanctions/export-control screening, BU export-control POCs, EUS and sanctions clauses; contingency planning for critical materials, routes, logistics providers and warehousing; rebalance MRO capacity and collaborate with OEMs on duty exemptions; insurance, hedging and geopolitical BCP scenarios; strategic partnerships with strong financial backing.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Roll out trade-compliance e-learning for relevant staff on evolving geopolitical and export-control requirements.

themes.themeName: Over Dependence on Key Vendors, OEMs and/or Single Source Suppliers
themes.sheetDetail: Late/non-delivery by key vendors, OEMs or single-source suppliers; OEM vertical integration and aftermarket consolidation increasing dependency on OEM-controlled IP, technical data, repair rights and licensing; rising material costs, rare-earth constraints and limited Tier-2/Tier-3 concentration visibility.
themes.sheetExtra: Vendor qualification and financial screening; regular performance reviews, site visits and delivery monitoring; strategic partnership agreements for IP, technical data, spares and support; alternative sourcing/subcontracting; safety stock and inventory buffers; design policy to avoid sole-source OEM components where possible.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Track OEM dependency/partnership by major engine and component and strengthen strategic partnerships; identify critical sub-tier, country and single-source dependencies and establish alternatives where feasible.

themes.sheetDetail: Customer financial difficulty from recession, withdrawal of government aid or aviation crisis; airline distress, low margins, high fuel prices and economic pressure; reliance on key customers across BUs may reduce bargaining power and amplify customer-loss impact.
themes.sheetExtra: Bi-weekly credit reviews and risk tiering using market/internal intelligence and early-warning indicators; segment customers by exposure and risk; monitor debts and intensify dunning, late-payment interest, legal warnings and COD terms; liens or sale-and-leaseback where appropriate; negotiate payment/commercial terms; review customer portfolio and concentration; long-term contracts, JVs and customer-feedback monitoring; diversify customers, products, programmes, services and partnerships.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Strengthen customer retention and credit management through customer feedback, follow-up actions, programme-performance reviews and improved credit terms; strengthen key-account management through Top/Grow/Build 15; develop an OEM engagement framework for major OEM customers and concentration exposure.

themes.themeName: Lack of Qualified and Experienced Technical Personnel
themes.sheetDetail: Competition for a limited pool of qualified aviation personnel; difficulty recruiting locals and foreign-worker quotas; high technician attrition driven by career and compensation factors; AI deployment requires job redesign and workforce upskilling; global technician shortages, retirements and long training/licensing lead times.
themes.sheetExtra: Use skilled subcontract labour for immediate needs; broaden analysis beyond Singapore; partner authorities/labour agents and technical institutions; ITE Engine Learning Centre; technical training programmes in Singapore, USA, China and Germany; intern incentives; track vacancy/time-to-fill and succession depth; annual Airframe workforce-development review; overseas/local institution collaboration.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Support BUs in job redesign, upskilling/reskilling, change management, AI competency development and AI-related talent acquisition; facilitate workforce integration and track AI competency against Group target.

themes.sheetDetail: Staff lapse or complacency; AI- and quantum-enabled threats, including deepfake phishing, malicious prompt injection and forged OEM certifications targeting SUP; aviation ransomware and extortion campaigns.
themes.sheetExtra: Cyber e-learning and GISO/CA ITBP publicity; GIO/GISO compliance for new or upgraded systems; IT-disruption BCP; cybersecurity roadmap including firewall, EDR, privileged-access management and vulnerability scanning; AI governance framework and training; N2 framework, policies and common platform; AIRMS and AI-governance e-learning.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Roll out Zero Trust Architecture and passwordless authentication for IBUs; align N2 projects with N2 OT/IoT Policy; minimise external file-sharing platforms; implement 2FA/MFA; strengthen suspicious-activity reporting.

themes.themeName: Legal & Regulatory Compliance (e.g., Sanctions, Trade Compliance, intermediaries)
themes.sheetDetail: Increasingly complex sanctions and trade-compliance environment; inconsistent BU/function understanding creating misaligned strategies and controls; lack of dedicated compliance personnel.
themes.sheetExtra: Due-diligence screening of customers, suppliers and intermediaries through Compliance Catalyst/Ethixbase; KYC checks for Russian-related and other restricted parties; quarterly tracking of reported fines; regular regulatory review and consistent practices through BCM annual review; external legal advice for potentially higher-risk projects.
themes.sheetActionPlans: Continuous monitoring and review of regulatory developments and trends.

themes.themeName: Foreign Exchange and Interest Rate Fluctuation
themes.sheetDetail: Interest-rate exposure, including AAM funding; foreign-currency cash-flow exposure.
themes.sheetExtra: Group Treasury central hedging strategy; AAM funding sourced in consultation with Treasury and hedged under Group interest-rate policy; BUs monitor cash-flow projections and work with Group Treasury on internal/external hedging under Group FX policy.

themes.sheetDetail: Workplace risks requiring systematic identification, assessment and mitigation.
themes.sheetExtra: WSH management systems covering risk assessments, incident reporting/investigation, training, emergency preparedness, audits and management reviews; ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 certified systems; regular internal/external audits and continual improvement.

themes.sheetDetail: Potential misalignment in joint ventures and associates, including applicability of newer Group policies such as AI governance.
themes.sheetExtra: Continuous evaluation of JVs and associates for ongoing partnership relevance; alignment to Group policies, including AI governance where applicable.

themes.themeName: Business Continuity Disruption due to extreme weather events and pandemic
themes.sheetDetail: Rising frequency of climate events, including heat stress, haze and flooding, plus potential pandemic recurrence, with possible operational disruption.
themes.sheetExtra: BCM controls and procedures to secure facilities and customer assets; hangars designed for harsher climate, including elevation and ventilation/cooling measures; insurance; early warnings; SOP/BCP measures; safe zones, backup power, drainage and emergency resources where applicable.

themes.themeName: Critical Emerging Technologies Disrupting Business Models
themes.sheetDetail: Potential disruption from hydrogen/electric/supersonic aircraft, AI and quantum technologies; need to align with evolving FAA/EASA AI certification expectations and next-generation aircraft/component/engine/nacelle capability.
themes.sheetExtra: IIoT/sensors for predictive maintenance; digital work cards/workflows; AI-driven preventive maintenance, planning and material provisioning; robotics, automation, digitalisation and analytics projects; A*STAR partnerships; R&D; CISO clearance of cyber projects; compliance with Group AI Governance policy.

themes.themeName: Evolving Workforce Demographics leading to Hiring and Retention Challenges
themes.sheetDetail: Ageing workforce and knowledge-transfer risk; skills mismatch as new technologies change roles; changing expectations of younger employees; diversity and inclusion needs; AI-driven organisation and job redesign.
themes.sheetExtra: Digital knowledge directories, continuous technical training, retired trainers, mature-worker upskilling, mentoring, internships/sponsorships; education partnerships, multiskilling, OTR, job redesign and succession planning; manager training; DI programmes and scorecards; Visier people analytics; AI Workforce Buildup Plan and ECMF.

themes.sheetDetail: Stricter GHG/emissions regulation; MRO process changes; aircraft redesign/retrofit and associated cost/timeline; compliance and carbon-footprint costs; customer demand for ESG practices and lower-carbon offerings.
themes.sheetExtra: ISO 14001/50001 certifications and DNV ESG accreditation work; ESG bid-requirement database; ISO 50001, ISO 14064-1 and GHG Protocol alignment; solar, rainwater, equipment electrification, SAF, OOA materials and recycling; quarterly resource/energy reporting; customer ESG-disclosure monitoring; workforce training and industry/regulator/supplier partnerships.

themes.themeName: OEM Aftermarket Growth: Licensing & Royalty Fee Implications
themes.sheetDetail: OEM aftermarket expansion may increase dependence on licensing, royalty arrangements, technical capabilities and access to OEM-controlled repair markets.
themes.sheetExtra: Technical training, capability development and knowledge transfer; leverage volume/consolidated purchasing; provision potential OEM royalties in customer pricing; strategic OEM partnerships/investments; specialised MRO expertise and market differentiation.
